metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 5–10% if price has not yet rebounded.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after recent rise or rises after recent fall), model often fails to recognize it; use 3-day moving average of past 10 days as a baseline for correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early days (first 5–7 days); apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 2–5% from forecast for days 1–7 if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.7 → -0.5 → +0.7), model may misread momentum; use sentiment swing amplitude as a multiplier for correction (e.g., if swing > 0.5, reduce forecast by 3–7%).
